newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hutchison Telecom starts HK fixed network service.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison Telecom starts HK fixed network service.

text.p: Hutchison Telecommunications (HK) Ltd said on Tuesday it had launched a fixed network service and was investing HK$6.2 billion in its development within the next five years.

The Hutchison Whampoa Ltd unit said its Network Eight On-Net Service would have a fibre optic backbone laid along Hong Kong's subway system and would feature the latest technology and a range of value-added services.
"In Hong Kong's competitive environment, offering the basics is not enough, we have to go beyond the basics," said Hutchison Telecom managing director Dennis Lui.
"Our heavy investments on the advanced technologies and equipment of the On-Net Service and the speedy progression of the network promises maximum cost effectiveness," he added.
The company was targetting 20,000 subscriber lines in 1997, said Brian To of the sales and marketing division.
Optical fibre cables have been laid to 29 of Hong Kong's 38 Mass Transit Railway (MTR) stations and would reach the remainder within next year, he said.
The company said its service was available at launch in high density areas such as the band from Sheung Wan to Quarry Bay on Hong Kong island along the MTR's Island Route.
Following completion of the MTR-based network, optical fibre rings would be further developed to provide coverage in the New Territories and the new airport at Chek Lap Kok, it said.
Hutchison Telecom is one of the three fixed-line network licensees which entered the market in mid-1995 when Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd's domestic monopoly ended.
The company is also involved in the mobile telephone, paging and international calling businesses.

Hutchison Telecom launched its International Direct Dial (IDD) service in 1995, which now has a customer base of some 300,000. It had an eight percent share of incoming IDD minutes, said executive director Patricia Leung.

Finance director Agnes Nardi said the wireless mobile business still provided more than half of the company's income and would likely continue to do so over the next three to five years. The rest would come from the paging and international businesses, she said.

The fixed-line network was still in the investment phase and may not be a major income generator for the time being, but the company was broadening its business to cope with rapid changes in the telecommunications market, company officials said.
